Hi!

I always wake up at the same time even without an alarm clock, regardless of when I went to bed. I've tried putting things in front of my clock in my room to make sure my body isn't glancing at it whilst sleeping to "know" when it's supposed to awake, but I still wake up at the same time.

How the hell does my body know exactly what time it is, even when it's sleeping?
How do humans "inner clock" work? [waking up at the same time every day]

Number of different factor. Some people's bodies weight different factors higher. 85% of it has to do with light and the release of melitonin when you are no longer seeing light. Fatigue plays a role, temperature plays a big role, caffine which turns off your ability to feel tired and whose pharmakenetics last longer than 16 hours plays a role and can take over the light exposure basis of the circadian rhythm, social aspects play a role.

Number one sleep tip, don't get too much sleep. Check out /v/mortalityrates. Sleep kills. The optimal for the average person is 7 hours... or less. The optimum is personal though.

As for waking up personally I can tell you that light plays a big part. I used to work nights and had to block out my windows. I tend to need pitch black to sleep. I could sleep for 13 hours if I wanted to. There was no natural trigger for wake up it seemed so I don't think it's entirely a timer that you start when you close your eyes.

Here's a panel talk on the science of sleep, if you're interested: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O0Uzy35uJzU

It covers with reasonable detail the biological clock.

I've found that when I go to bed wanting to wake up at a specific time in the morning, I usually do. If I set the alarm, I wake up a few minutes before it goes off. I don't know how it works but it comes in handy.
